name: Distance-preserving decomposition of an even spider
summary: A 2n-legged Z-spider is fault-equivalent to two n-legged spiders joined through n four-legged spiders.
description:
A phase-free Z-spider with $2n$ legs can be decomposed into two $n$-legged spiders and $n$ four-legged spiders: each four-legged spider carries two of the original legs and is connected to both of the $n$-legged spiders. The rewrite is distance-preserving (equivalently, fault-equivalent under edge-flip noise). Applied recursively, together with the four- and five-legged rules, it decomposes arbitrarily large spiders, and hence arbitrary-weight Pauli measurements, into spiders of degree at most three.

It is proven by unfusing a spider with [one-legged fusion](../fe-one-legged-fusion/), applying the [odd version](../fe-odd-spider-decomposition/), and fusing back.
parameter_notes: A spider with 2n legs, built from two n-legged spiders and n four-legged spiders (shown for n = 3); holds for any n ≥ 1.
